categories.name: Nano Aquariums
categories.tagline: Rimless tanks, lids and setup essentials
categories.description: Compact aquariums and the small but important pieces that go with them: leveling mats, lids and all-in-one kits sized for desks, shelves and countertops.
categories.intro: Nano aquariums — usually anything under about 10 gallons — are a popular way to start in the hobby, but small water volumes leave less margin for error. The equipment here focuses on stable, well-supported setups: properly leveled glass, lids that limit evaporation, and kits with filtration sized for the tank.
categories.photoAlt: A small cube aquarium with green plants glowing under a light in a dark room

categories.name: Shrimp Tank Essentials
categories.tagline: Gentle filtration, acclimation and water monitoring
categories.description: Equipment chosen around the needs of dwarf freshwater shrimp: gentle filtration, intake protection, slow acclimation and tools for tracking water parameters.
categories.intro: Dwarf shrimp such as Neocaridina and Caridina are small enough to be pulled into unprotected filter intakes and are sensitive to sudden changes in water chemistry. Shrimp-focused equipment is mostly about gentleness and consistency: sponge filtration, covered intakes, slow drip acclimation and reliable ways to measure what is in the water.
categories.photoAlt: A red cherry shrimp resting on a carpet of fine green aquarium plants

categories.name: Aquascaping Tools
categories.description: Precision planting and trimming tools, plus the substrate and hardscape materials that form the foundation of a planted layout.
categories.intro: Aquascaping tools let you plant, trim and adjust a layout without disturbing the whole tank. Long stainless tweezers place stems and small plants exactly where you want them, specialised scissors keep carpets and stem groups tidy, and a spatula smooths substrate slopes. This category also covers substrate and natural hardscape.
categories.photoAlt: An aquascaper using long tweezers to plant a small Anubias on driftwood underwater

categories.name: Filtration & Maintenance
categories.tagline: Filters, siphons, cleaners and test kits
categories.description: Filtration sized for small tanks and the maintenance tools that make routine water changes, glass cleaning and testing quicker.
categories.intro: Good filtration and a simple maintenance routine do most of the work of keeping a small aquarium stable. This category covers compact filters with adjustable flow, gravel siphons sized for nano tanks, glass cleaners and test kits for checking the nitrogen cycle and water hardness.
categories.photoAlt: A planted aquarium with glass lily pipes for filter intake and outflow on the right side

categories.name: Lighting & Equipment
categories.tagline: LED lights, heaters, pumps and thermometers
categories.description: Lighting, heating and air equipment for small freshwater aquariums, with an emphasis on controllable, appropriately sized hardware.
categories.intro: Lighting drives plant growth and how a tank looks, while heaters, thermometers and air pumps keep conditions steady. For nano tanks the key is proportion: lights with adjustable intensity and timers, heaters sized for small volumes, and quiet air pumps for sponge filters.
categories.photoAlt: A rimless planted aquarium lit by three pendant LED lights, with tetras swimming above a green carpet

products.name: Stainless Steel Aquascaping Tool Set, 5-Piece
products.summary: Two tweezers, two scissors and a substrate spatula in a roll-up case — the core kit for planting and trimming.
products.description: A five-piece set covering the jobs you do most often in a planted aquarium: placing stems and small plants, trimming carpets and stem groups, and shaping substrate. Each tool is roughly 25–27 cm long, which reaches the bottom of typical nano and medium-sized tanks while keeping your hand out of the water. The set stores in a zip-up roll case so the tips stay protected between maintenance sessions.
features: Straight tweezers (27 cm) for planting stems, pushing roots into substrate and placing moss
Curved tweezers (27 cm) for working around hardscape and reaching behind rocks and wood
Wave scissors (25 cm) for cutting stem plants and thinning dense growth
Curved scissors (25 cm) with a downward bend for trimming carpets close to the substrate
Flat substrate spatula (25 cm) for smoothing slopes and terraces
Brushed stainless steel finish and a zip-up storage case with elastic loops

specs.Storage: Zip-up roll case with elastic loops

tankSize.note: Comfortable for tanks up to about 30 cm (12 in) deep. Deeper tanks benefit from 38 cm or longer tools.

suitableFor: Planting a new nano or medium aquascape
Routine trimming of stem plants and carpets
Shrimp tanks where you want to rearrange moss and plants without netting animals
Smoothing and re-sloping substrate after maintenance
pros: Covers planting, trimming and substrate work in one set
Lengths suit the most common nano and medium tank depths
Curved scissors make carpet trimming more practical than straight blades
Roll case protects tips and keeps the set together
limitations: 27 cm tweezers are short for tanks deeper than about 30 cm
Stainless steel can still spot or tarnish if stored wet — rinse and dry after use
Tweezer tips are sharp; work slowly around shrimp and fish
No spring scissors included for very fine carpet work

products.name: Active Plant & Shrimp Soil, 3 L
products.summary: Granular aqua soil that softens water and supports rooted plants.
products.description: An active (buffering) aqua soil made from baked granules. Active soils lower and stabilise pH and carbonate hardness, which suits soft-water plants and Caridina shrimp. Like most active soils, it can release ammonia during the first weeks underwater, so the tank should be fully cycled and tested before shrimp are added.
features: Granular soil that supports root growth
Buffers water toward slightly acidic, soft conditions
Dark colour that contrasts well with green plants
3 L bag sized for a typical 5-gallon footprint

specs.Coverage: Approx. 4 cm deep in a 36 × 22 cm tank

tankSize.note: One bag covers a typical 5-gallon footprint. Larger tanks need multiple bags.

pros: Supports rooted plants without separate capping
Helps keep pH stable in soft-water setups
Fine granules make planting with tweezers easy
limitations: May release ammonia during initial weeks — cycle before adding livestock
Buffering capacity is gradually used up and soil eventually needs replacing
Lower pH may not suit every species; check your livestock's preferred range
Granules can break down if disturbed often

Good anchor surface for mosses and epiphyte plants

An air pump lifts water through the uplift tube, drawing it gently through the sponges where beneficial bacteria colonise. Because there is no impeller intake, shrimp — including newborns — can safely graze on the sponge surface.

Weighted base keeps the filter upright
Sponges can be rinsed separately to preserve bacteria

specs.Requires: Air pump and airline tubing (not included)

tankSize.note: Use a check valve on the airline if the pump sits below the water line.

suitableFor: Seeding bacteria for a backup filter
limitations: Needs a separate air pump
Bubbling is audible in quiet rooms
Takes up visible space in a small tank
Less mechanical polishing than a canister or HOB filter

products.name: Digital TDS Meter with Temperature Readout
products.summary: Quick pocket readings of total dissolved solids — handy for remineralising RO water.
products.description: A pen-style meter that estimates total dissolved solids (TDS) from electrical conductivity. Shrimp keepers commonly use TDS readings to check remineralised RO water and to see whether tank water is drifting between water changes. TDS does not identify what is dissolved, so it complements rather than replaces GH, KH and nitrogen tests.
limitations: Does not tell you which substances are dissolved
Should be checked against calibration solution periodically
Not a substitute for ammonia, nitrite and nitrate tests
